newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Pakistan has agreed to extradite more than a dozen Iranians wanted by the Iranian government for their alleged involvement in criminal activities.
- The Afghan government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani has informed Pakistan that it will welcome a Pakistani mission due to arrive in Kabul on Thursday, the Afghan Islamic Press said.

- Differences have arisen between Punjab province and Islamabad on financing what many believe to be a politically carved-out urban development package of 114.13 billion rupees announced last week by Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
- One M-163 mine-hunter, named Mohafiz, will be formlly inducted into the Pakistan Navy at a ceremony in Karachi on Wednesday.
- The main opposition Pakistan Muslim League party has requisitioned a session of the National Assembly with a one-point agenda - setting up an accountability commission.
THE NEWS
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday the opposition would file a petition in the Supreme Court against what he called "corrupt rulers".
- Pakistan was unanimously elected as the vice-president of the 51st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
- Pakistani authorities decided to set up a new camp outside the northwestern town of Peshawar to house refugees fleeing from fresh factional fighting in eastern Afghanistan.
- The first consignment of a total of 1.8 million tonnes of imported wheat will arrive at Port Qasim on September 22.
- Pakistan government's internal and external debt was estimated at 1,700 billion rupees in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June).
- The ruling Pakistan Democratic Front has finally decided to hold local bodies' elections in Punjab province on non-party basis.
THE MUSLIM
- Foreign Secretary Najmuddin Sheikh leaves for Kabul on Thursday to meet Afghan officials and open Pakistani mission in a new building provided by President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government.
- Pakistan and Oman plan to enhance defence cooperation.

- The Afghan government said it had struck an accord with northern warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum to face the Taleban Islamic militia, but the claim was later denied by Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli party.
THE NATION
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday that Pakistan was on the verge of defaulting on debt repayments.

- The proposed establishment of about 13 tax-free industrial zones in Sindh province remains in the doldrums as the International Monetary Fund has declined to provide funds for any tax-free project in Pakistan.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Pakistani government may impose regulatory duty on the import of edible oil if the prices of vegetable ghee are not reduced by the private sector.
- The contractors of Ghazi Barotha hydro-power project are planning to sue the state-run Water and Power Development Authority to claim damages for delay in the release of their machinery.
FINANCIAL POST
- Japan Power Generations Ltd, a Pakistani private power firm, is planning to offer a capital of 138 million rupees to the public in the form of shares.
- Fifteen percent of construction work on 586-megawatt Uch Power project has been completed.
- The Asian Development Bank chief in Islamabad has expressed concern over low performance of contractors engaged in various ADB-financed projects in Pakistan.
- Walnut-sized hailstones lashed the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad making tiny dents on hundreds of cars.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
